title: mini-onramp-funnels-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- We need lightweight funnels to get new users to reliable assistant interactions quickly: reduce friction, demonstrate value within 1–3 turns, and collect signals for personalization and evals.
- Existing onboarding is broad (credits, SDK examples) but not tailored to conversational surfaces; drop-off is highest during first query/response.

Goal (north star):
- 35% higher 3-turn retention for new users who go through a conversational mini-onramp vs control over 30 days.
- Surface high-signal telemetry for prompt-eval pairing and early quality regressions.

Constraints / principles:
- Friction-first: minimal required inputs from users; default personas/templates should work out of the box.
- Safety-by-default: any suggested prompts or templates must run through existing safety checks and be editable before sending.
- Incremental personalization: prefer ephemeral session-level signals initially (no long-term storage without opt-in).
- Quick experiments: toggles at route level, trackable via per-route telemetry.

Target users / segments:
- Developer sandbox users (first-time API key use)
- Product trial users experimenting with assistant/chat features
- Platform teams trying demo flows for stakeholders

Proposed mini-onramp variants (high-level):
1) Guided micro-journey (A): 3-step flow — pick use-case template (e.g., "summarize docs"), customize one-line instruction, run sample convo.
2) Prompt-playground (B): interactive template with suggested follow-ups and "improve this prompt" quick action.
3) Persona-tryout (C): pick persona tone + sample prompts that highlight different latency/cost tradeoffs (compact vs verbose).
4) Zero-config quickstart (D): single button run with default prompt and immediate example metrics (tokens, time, model variant).

User stories (examples):
- As a sandbox dev, I want an opinionated sample that shows value in two replies so I can justify further integration.
- As a PM, I want to compare two onramp variants' retention so I can pick the best for the sales demo funnel.
- As a security-conscious engineer, I want to see what fields are tracked and opt-out options.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- New route /onramp/{variant} serves the UI + example request templates.
- Telemetry events emitted: onramp_shown, onramp_chosen_variant, onramp_submit, onramp_edit_template, onramp_opt_out.
- Basic A/B wiring: can target user cohorts by newness flag and company size.
- Safety check runs: template suggestions validated through safety pipeline before being editable.

Metrics to instrument (first 30 days):
- 3-turn retention (major metric)
- conversion to persisted integration (API or SDK usage within 7 days)
- avg tokens per session, median latency, throughput (sdk vs playground)
- percent users who edit template before submit
- OSS: quality regressions surfaced via micro-evals seeded from onramp prompts

Experiment matrix (quick sketch):
- Variants: A, B, C, D (see above)
- Cohorts: new_user (first 7 days), trial_user (company trial), returning_dev
- Metrics: retention@3, integration_rate@7, edit_rate, avg_cost_per_demo
- Success threshold: +20% integration_rate and +35% retention@3 to promote variant from experiment to default.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0: internal alpha (team-only) — manual toggles, feature flag RED.onramp.alpha, ~2 weeks.
- Phase 1: controlled beta — 5% of new users, collect metrics and heatmaps, 4 weeks.
- Phase 2: wider rollout by cohort (trial accounts), 2–4 weeks.
- Phase 3: default in sandbox for all new accounts with opt-out.

Telemetry & logging notes (implementation):
- Emit route-level events with anonymized cohort_id, variant_id, model_used, request_time_ms, token_count.
- Persist prompt templates used (hash & bucket) rather than raw prompt text unless user opts in to share for eval.
- Attach micro-eval hooks: sample a subset of onramp interactions to run downstream quality checks and flag regressions.

Privacy / compliance considerations:
- Default behavior: do not store raw user prompts beyond 24 hours unless user opts in.
- If a customer account requests retention for trial debugging, require explicit consent flow and KMS policy.

Open design questions / tradeoffs:
- How opinionated should templates be? (higher conversion vs more personalization/friction)
- Short-term storage for evals: store hashed prompts + embeddings vs raw text with masking?
- Should onramp variants expose cost/latency tradeoffs transparently to end users or hide complexity?

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: suggested prompts accidentally surface PII patterns — Mitigate: safety pipeline + redact UI preview + opt-in.
- Risk: adding onramp increases first-call cost — Mitigate: default to low-cost model variant with clear switch to higher-quality option.
- Risk: telemetry noise from curious users — Mitigate: cohort sampling + smoothing logic for metrics.

Prototype checklist (engineering + design):
- [ ] Minimal UI shell and 4 variants wired to feature flags
- [ ] Backend endpoints for template generation + safety checks
- [ ] Telemetry events & A/B config in experimentation service (RED-4312)
- [ ] E2E tests: safety, opt-out, event emission
- [ ] Quick demo script for internal alpha and decks for PM/CS to test

Next steps (short-term):
- Sync with design (Ava) to produce microcopy and 3 sample templates per variant — due 10/18.
- Spike: implement telemetry hook + hashed-prompt storage — assign to Kai for 1-week spike.
- Schedule 30-min sync with CS to collect trial account personas to prioritize templates.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep flow < 90s from landing to first useful reply.
- Track 'did_edit_template' as a strong signal of engagement/curiosity.
- Consider a follow-up email to users who complete onramp with resources and sample SDK snippet.

Slack threads / tickets to scan before next sync:
- #product-onboarding (thread pinned: onramp proposal)
plaintext_preview: Quick draft: mini onramp funnels (3-turn retention goal, variants A-D, telemetry events, rollout phases, acceptance criteria, risks).
